details: Malicious package. `@leonoremods/baileys` is a trojanized fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library (@whiskeysockets/baileys). It ships a hardcoded default list of attacker-controlled WhatsApp channels and, by default, issues authenticated `w:mex` newsletter FOLLOW mutations that silently subscribe the victim account to all of them. In 1.10.1 the list is `DEFAULT_AUTO_FOLLOW_CHANNELS` in `lib/Defaults/index.js`, followed on the first successful connection: 120363407849633830@newsletter, 120363409911086003@newsletter, 120363412456119539@newsletter, 120363424810646424@newsletter, 120363429677187777@newsletter, 120363431638412364@newsletter, 120363431951214986@newsletter. In 1.2.9 the list is in `src/WAUSync/Protocols/USyncNewsletterProtocol.js` (the same channels except 120363431638412364@newsletter), followed on timers 50 to 100 seconds after the socket is created. In 1.10.1, `lib/Socket/luxu.js`, imported by `messages-send.js`, additionally stamps outgoing event and poll-result messages with forwarded-newsletter context naming channel 120363421563597486@newsletter. Legitimate Baileys never hardcodes a channel JID or auto-follows a channel. Versions 1.2.9 and 1.10.1 carry this code; the `0.0.0-stage` placeholder does not.
